items.title: “Escuelita means “little school.” …”
items.where: The New Age May Dawn Suddenly, P6
items.my_version: That’s where the ***escuelita*** in my title comes in. Escuelita means “little school.” I’m borrowing the word from the Zapatistas in Mexico, whose *Escuelita* had outsiders stay with Zapatista families for a while and learn self-government by taking part in everyday life. In the same way, people would live in the healing communities I’m proposing, to heal and to learn the relational and practical methods, so that some of them could eventually leave and set up another one somewhere else. Otherwise, we’ve built a lovely refuge for whoever got there first.

items.title: “I was usually just a visitor’s kid …”
items.where: The New Age May Dawn Suddenly, P12
items.my_version: I spent much of my childhood being carried through Twin Oaks, Acorn, East Wind, Padanaram, Zendik, and many other communities. I was usually just a visitor’s kid. I could see how people lived, but I was never really part of the tribe. At the time, that meant a lot of boredom, with some adventures mixed in, but those years gave me a great sample to compare against.

items.title: “We evolved to live in small groups …”
items.your_version: What’s starving them is anomie. We evolved to live in small groups where everybody knows, loves, and trusts everybody. In a large society, the shared norms and close ties that held those groups together fall apart, and nobody knows anybody well enough or for long enough to tell who can be trusted--even your next-door neighbor is often a total stranger. That’s how large societies end up run by psychopaths. (Yes, I’m always going on about this.)
